# Forms of support and administrative contributions

Choose the support arrangement, define its scope and apply the administrative contribution.

**Operational framework approved by JF on 19 October 2026. Documentation owner: Laura. Financial application: CFO.**

Use this framework when accepting an initiative, agreeing a programme or allocating a receipt. Read it with the applicable agreement and the [RACI](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle). Existing agreements and valid amendments govern their own scope; this page does not retrospectively change them or replace specialist legal or tax review.

#### Choose the form of support

| Arrangement                                 | OCE's role                                                                                                                         | Scope to establish                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hosting an initiative or collective         | Receive funding, maintain the budget record, check supporting evidence and process eligible expenses.                              | Standard hosting serves an initiative without separate legal personality. The collective leads its activities. Apply the mandate requirements for its funding.                    |
| A support fund for an existing organisation | Receive and allocate funding intended for an independent organisation, control onward transfers and follow the agreed obligations. | Identify the recipient, purpose, agreement, authorised transfers and reporting. The organisation remains independent; this is not unrestricted banking or automatic pass-through. |
| Administration of a fund or programme       | Administer multiple receipts, agreed governance, grant agreements, programme operations and reporting.                             | Define programme decisions, OCE's controls, workload, reporting, personnel or external support, and the contribution in writing.                                                  |

These are operating arrangements, not automatic legal classifications or three contribution tiers. A profile called “Friends of” does not establish its contractual model.

Crowdfunding, institutional grants and Myriad are funding routes across these arrangements. Receiving a grant does not create a fourth form of support. A programme can combine hosted initiatives and onward grants, provided the responsibilities and funding flows are clear.

#### Define what is included

The usual scope covers application review and onboarding, the appropriate financial record, identified receipts and allocations, routine evidence and funding-condition checks, authorised payments or grants, traceability and ordinary support.

The initiative or programme provides its activity plan, programme budget, supporting documents, field information and the approvals required by its agreement. OCE performs its own controls and the obligations it has accepted. Programme approval does not replace OCE's checks.

For each grant or programme, agree who prepares the narrative, validates the financial information, submits the report and tracks each deadline. Reporting already required by the agreement belongs to that agreed scope.

Agree separately before committing to dedicated personnel or payroll, extensive bespoke agreements, specially developed reporting, an external audit, impact evaluation, complete fundraising applications, event delivery, ticketing or sales, unusual onward-grant routes and specialist tools. Record the work, owner, resources and funding. Do not charge corrective work caused by OCE's own errors as an additional assignment.

Do not promise universal tax deductibility, unlimited legal or tax advice, payment cards for all collectives, cash advances, investment returns or successful fundraising. [Public funding](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/receiving-funds-from-europe) remains subject to a case decision.

Existing operational commitments continue: a [first application response](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review) within seven business days, and [payment execution](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/financial-ops-task-overview) within seven business days after collective-administrator approval, with notification when a problem prevents execution. These are not promises of final admission or beneficiary receipt within that period.

#### Select the applicable contribution

Use **administrative contribution** in communications. It supports OCE's team, controls and shared infrastructure.

The [public administrative-contribution table](https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate#administrative-contributions) is the single reference for standard rates. Payment-provider charges, currency conversion and applicable taxes are distinct. Do not describe the standard crowdfunding arrangement as a guaranteed all-inclusive percentage.

Check the current signed agreement and valid amendments before applying a rate, fixed amount, cap, exemption or minimum. An existing particular rate is not a new exception each time it is applied. A new departure from standard rates requires JF's approval and the existing exception record.

For a new fund or programme, use the standard grant contribution as the starting reference, then assess its scope and cost before agreement. A percentage does not imply unlimited work. Changes to existing arrangements follow their amendment, notice and effective-date requirements.

#### Classify funding before the payment method

Crowdfunding covers contributions without particular funding conditions in an identifiable Open Collective campaign. A bank transfer initiated or reconciled within that contribution journey can belong to crowdfunding: retain the contribution reference or other evidence of that link. A campaign name in a bank memo alone is insufficient.

A grant remains a grant even if paid by card or recorded on the platform. A bank donation outside the crowdfunding journey uses the standard non-crowdfunding rule. Resolve ambiguity before promising a net amount.

This boundary was approved on 19 October 2026. Apply it consistently with the agreement in force; align contractual wording and required notices before changing an existing arrangement. Do not retrospectively reclassify receipts through a documentation edit.

#### Calculate and record the allocation

**Establish the base**

Unless the applicable agreement specifies another base, calculate the contribution on the gross funding actually awarded and received by OCE for the project, before OCE's contribution and the processing charges on that receipt. Evidence must distinguish the gross funding, withheld charges and net bank credit.

An expected grant, donation pledge or balance still held by an intermediary is not cash received by OCE.

For Myriad or another intermediary, use the grant awarded and transferred to OCE, before charges on that transfer. Do not automatically use the donor's original contribution to the intermediary. Show upstream costs separately and do not deduct them again. Follow [the Myriad workflow](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/myriad-usa) for request, receipt and reporting.

Apply the contribution once to the incoming funding within the agreed scope. An internal allocation, currency transfer or onward grant already covered by that scope does not automatically trigger another contribution. If a recipient enters another hosting arrangement or legal entity, check and explain any separate contribution before commitment.

**Keep other amounts distinct**

* **Payment and transfer costs:** identify actual charges and allocate them under the agreement, without duplicate deductions or undisclosed markup. Record any cost absorbed by OCE.
* **Currency conversion:** retain the source-currency calculation, actual conversion evidence and allocation in the destination currency. Credit the net proceeds actually obtained, not a theoretical spot-rate amount. Do not deduct conversion costs already included in those proceeds again. Follow [incoming transfers](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives).
* **Taxes:** the term “administrative contribution” does not determine tax treatment. Distinguish taxation of OCE's contribution from taxes on programme operations or suppliers. CFO coordinates the treatment with Saïd or the competent adviser.
* **Interest:** apply the particular agreement and documented authorised decisions. No universal allocation percentage or guaranteed return is created. Interest is not automatically another donation subject to the standard contribution.
* **Platform tips:** optional tips support Ofico, not OCE. Donors may change or remove their tip. Keep it separate from OCE's contribution; the existing host-level setting remains applicable.

**Use the existing grant-entry procedure**

Follow [the grant receipt checklist](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives#grant-receipt-checklist-net-allocation-and-administrative-contribution). For manually allocated grants, create and verify both required Add Funds entries: the net allocation to the beneficiary collective and the retained administrative contribution to the correct OCE operating budget. Link both to the same receipt and calculation, without an additional automatic platform contribution.

Financial review must identify the relevant ADDED\_FUNDS entries as well as HOST\_FEE records. Not every ADDED\_FUNDS entry is OCE's own income. A platform category does not determine accounting or tax classification.

**Cancellations and refunds**

Subject to applicable particular terms, adjust the administrative contribution proportionally when incoming funding is cancelled in whole or in part. Identify any non-recoverable third-party costs separately. An expense repayment to a project budget is not new incoming funding subject to another contribution.

Routine refund decisions remain within the existing delegations; this rule creates no blanket prior-approval requirement.

#### Worked examples

These examples illustrate the standard rules, assume no additional tax and do not replace a particular agreement.

| Situation                                                                                                                     | Calculation                                                                      | Available project budget |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Crowdfunding contribution of EUR 1,000; actual processing cost EUR 20                                                         | EUR 80 administrative contribution + EUR 20 processing                           | EUR 900                  |
| Grant of EUR 100,000; EUR 100 receipt charges borne by the project                                                            | EUR 10,000 administrative contribution + EUR 100 charges; bank credit EUR 99,900 | EUR 89,900               |
| Donor gives USD 100,000 to an intermediary; it awards and transfers USD 95,000 to OCE after its own costs; no further charges | OCE contribution USD 9,500 on the USD 95,000 grant                               | USD 85,500               |

The intermediary example does not establish that any provider always charges 5%. Confirm its actual conditions.

#### Cost a substantial programme

Before a substantial new commitment or renewal, Laura estimates the work and CFO assesses the cost: staff time at its loaded cost, a share of support functions and programme-specific expenditure. Exclude amounts already financed elsewhere from any additional recovery.

Use a prudent funding assumption. If the percentage covers the scope, retain it. Otherwise reduce the scope, explicitly fund additional resources or agree a programme-specific minimum. There is no universal minimum or hourly contribution schedule.

Where a minimum is agreed for a period, the total contribution is the **higher of the agreed percentage and the agreed minimum**, not their sum. An illustrative EUR 12,000 minimum against a calculated EUR 10,000 contribution produces a EUR 2,000 top-up. Specify the period, funding assumptions, settlement and costs included before commitment.

A separate fixed contribution may fund an additional assignment clearly outside the base scope. Define its deliverables and avoid recovering the same work twice.

Solidarity between initiatives is possible when the support is explicit, financed and compatible with OCE's capacity. This does not require identical cost recovery from every small collective. For substantial programmes, make the resources committed and contribution to the shared infrastructure visible.

#### Responsibilities and working record

Use the [RACI](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle):

* Laura qualifies the arrangement, coordinates complex funds, defines reporting and assigns the work.
* Ivan checks evidence, performs routine operations and records allocations.
* CFO reviews calculations, reconciliation and sustainability, and coordinates accounting and tax matters with Saïd.
* JF decides policy, new rate departures and material commitments. Reserved decisions remain with the Board.

A complex programme already within an agreed framework does not require JF's approval for every routine transaction.

Keep the following in the existing project record: contracting entity, support model, operational owner, agreement and amendments, contribution and base, currency, timing, effective date, third-party costs, interest rule, authorised expenditure or transfers, reporting, scope limits and exit conditions. Reuse Open Collective, the grant application and the supporting Drive dossier.

#### Implementation and maintenance

The framework and calculation rules were approved by JF for internal documentation on 19 October 2026. Specialist financial procedures, legal and tax validation, contract alignment and actual programme cost reviews remain separate implementation work. Publication does not itself complete the professionalisation milestone.

Laura maintains this page; CFO confirms financial application. Link to the public standard-rate table rather than reproducing competing contribution schedules. Align general website wording and contractual templates through their appropriate update process.

This handbook is currently public. Keep negotiated partner terms, identifiable financial cases, signatures and private evidence in restricted records. Use anonymous examples here.


# Support collectives

Find the workflow and keep a clear next action for the person asking.

Support combines practical assistance with care for the person’s circumstances. Start by understanding what they need, the collective involved and the action they are trying to complete.

## Choose the process

* [Handle a support request](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/support-best-practices).
* [Review an application](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review).
* [Run an onboarding conversation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/the-onboarding-call).
* [Check an operational action](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/operational-checklist-mandatory-before-action).
* [Review a restriction or closure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/freezing-collectives).

## Communicate a useful next step

Explain what has been checked, what is needed and who will act next. Use short paragraphs and plain language. Avoid making someone repeat sensitive information already held in the case record.

Keep open work visible. Sending a reply is not the same as resolving a case. If the issue needs another role, hand over the context, next action and deadline.

Use the [public collective guide](https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/) when pointing someone to general instructions; keep case-specific decisions and private evidence in restricted systems. Freshdesk is the reference for the support request’s owner, next action and resolution; see the support procedure above.


# Handle a support request

Take ownership of a request, find the right answer and follow it through in Freshdesk.

#### Purpose and scope

Use this procedure when a collective asks for help or reports a platform problem. The result is a resolved request with evidence of the outcome, or an open request with a named owner and a clear next action.

For a new hosting application, use [Review an application](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review). For a safety or misconduct concern, follow [Safeguarding response](/oc-europe-internal-doc/human-resources-introduction/detailed-guidance-for-staff-on-responding-to-safeguarding-issues) and its restricted reporting route.

#### Who is responsible?

**Ivan is accountable for routine support and platform problems.** He triages new support tickets in Freshdesk and ensures that each has a named owner. **When Ivan is absent, Laura handles this triage and ensures that new tickets have a named owner.** Ivan or the team member taking the case performs the work. Laura coordinates allocation, priorities and cover. These responsibilities come from the [adopted operational RACI](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle), particularly rows 12 and 15.

Asking someone for a decision does not transfer ownership of the request. If another person takes over, leave the context, evidence and next action.

#### Before you start

**Freshdesk is the reference for the request’s owner, next action and resolution.** Check the existing ticket before replying or creating a duplicate. Read relevant previous correspondence, including email where needed.

Make sure you can access the ticket and the records needed for your work. If access is missing, ask Ivan; if ownership or cover is unclear, ask Laura. Access to a tool does not itself authorise a payment or decision.

Keep case evidence in restricted systems. This public handbook contains the procedure, not individual support cases.

#### 1. Understand and record the request

Identify:

* The collective and its fiscal host or legal entity.
* What the person is trying to do and what is preventing it.
* The relevant expense, profile or transaction reference, if applicable.
* What has already been tried and whether another person is handling it.
* The named case owner and the next action.

Keep this context in the Freshdesk ticket, with links to supporting records where access is appropriate. Avoid asking someone to repeat sensitive information already held in the case record.

#### 2. Find the applicable procedure

Read the relevant GitBook procedure and the applicable agreement. Do not rely on a remembered response or a saved template alone.

For platform questions, separate these checks:

| Check              | What to establish                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Account and access | Is the person using the expected account, with the necessary permissions?                                            |
| Interface          | Which action is missing or failing? Check the [platform documentation](https://documentation.opencollective.com/).   |
| OCE decision       | Is approval, further evidence or a policy clarification needed? A platform capability does not supply that approval. |

If sources conflict, record the precise question and obtain the appropriate decision before taking the affected action.

#### 3. Resolve the issue or ask for a decision

For routine work within your authority, apply the relevant procedure. Before a payment, agreement or consequential instruction, use [Check before an operational action](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/operational-checklist-mandatory-before-action).

If the issue needs another role, send the facts, relevant evidence, the specific question, a recommended option where possible, and the date by which a decision is needed:

* **Laura:** priorities, allocation of work, working arrangements and project commitments.
* **CFO:** balances, accounting, reconciliation, VAT or uncertain financial treatment.
* **JF:** material commitments, genuine exceptions or legal and reputational risk.
* **Safety or misconduct:** use the safeguarding procedure, including its alternative route when the usual contact is involved.

Pause the affected action while its basis is unresolved; continue unaffected information gathering. Missing documents normally call for a targeted request, not automatic escalation to executive direction. See [Risk and escalation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/risk-and-compliance).

#### 4. Reply with a manageable next step

Explain what you checked, what happens next and who will act. Use everyday language and short paragraphs.

If a document is needed, explain why. If the person cannot provide it, understand the obstacle and escalate the actual question instead of repeating the same demand.

For a technical instruction, explain how the person can tell that it worked. If a screenshot is needed, request only the relevant area and ask them to omit credentials and unrelated personal details.

**When using a saved response**

**Ivan maintains the response templates in Freshdesk.** Report an outdated or incorrect template to Ivan, identifying the wording and the applicable procedure. Template maintenance does not authorise a change to the underlying policy; use the decision routes above when a rule needs clarification or approval.

Use the response templates in Freshdesk. Before sending, adapt the wording to the request and check the host, legal entity, contact address, signature and next action. A saved response does not replace the applicable procedure or agreement.

Application responses must follow the [current administrator and follow-up rules](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review). Do not override the documented one-administrator exception or introduce an automatic closure deadline. Keep approved rules in GitBook and reusable response wording in Freshdesk.

#### 5. Keep follow-up visible

**When waiting for the collective, the ticket owner decides when and how to follow up, case by case.** Keep the next action visible in Freshdesk and record any planned follow-up date. There is no fixed reminder schedule for these requests.

Record the outstanding action and its owner in Freshdesk. A requested document, sent instruction or pending payment may still require follow-up. Preserve any agreed deadline and leave enough context for a colleague to continue the work.

**Response times:** no standard first-response target is currently formalised for routine support. Track each request’s next action and any deadline agreed for that case. Hosting applications follow a separate rule: an initial response within seven business days.

#### 6. Verify the outcome before closing

Record what resolved the request and the supporting reference. For a missing-payment case, sending instructions alone is not evidence of resolution.

If work remains, keep the outstanding action and owner visible. If another person takes over, record the handover and next step. A reply sent is not, by itself, a completed case.

#### Case-note checklist

Use this as a content checklist in the existing Freshdesk ticket; it does not require a new form or duplicate register.

* **Context:** collective, host/entity and relevant reference.
* **Request:** desired outcome and observed problem.
* **Checks:** procedure, evidence reviewed and action already taken.
* **Ownership:** case owner; decision needed and person asked, if any.
* **Next step:** action, person responsible and any agreed deadline.
* **Outcome:** resolution evidence or remaining work.

#### Sources and maintenance

Operational responsibilities: [Operational RACI](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle).

**Still to clarify:** exact Freshdesk queue/status conventions.


# Check before an operational action

A short control point before a payment, agreement or consequential instruction.

Use the checks relevant to the action. Verification is part of the work; an AI review does not replace it.

## Identity and scope

* Correct collective, legal entity and currency.
* Correct recipient and authority to act.
* Relevant agreement and any documented exception reviewed.

## Financial action

* Amount and purpose match the supporting evidence.
* Required approvals and documents are present.
* Payee and payout details match, or the specific exception is authorised.
* Funds and the intended payment route are available.
* No duplicate or unresolved previous attempt remains.

## Agreement or instruction

* Correct template, recipient and current platform settings.
* No unapproved commitment or assumption about eligibility.
* Clear wording and a practical next action.
* Private information is shared only through the appropriate channel.

## If something is unresolved

Pause the affected action, record the specific issue and route it to the competent person. A high amount alone is not proof of an exception; assess the actual deviation and risk.

## After execution

Retain the outcome, reference and evidence. If there is an error, examine the control and conditions that allowed it; do not assume that the existence of a checklist proves the cause.

See [AI use](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce/ai-usage-policy) and [risk and escalation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/risk-and-compliance).


# Review an application

Track the application from first information to a recorded decision.

## Intake and current sources

Application review combines information from Open Collective, Freshdesk, forms and Slack. Laura maintains the existing “Application Follow-Up” document in Superhuman Docs, originally created by Gwen, as the shared record of application progress, decisions and the reasons for acceptance or refusal.

| Route              | Where Laura starts                                  | Additional checks                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| OCE                | Applications on Open Collective                     | Check Freshdesk for previous exchanges or replies and whether the collective completed the Typeform.                                                    |
| Open Source Europe | Lucas's comments and AI-generated comments in Slack | Where needed, check Freshdesk exchanges and Typeform responses, or the replacement form Lucas is finalising. Confirm which form is in use for the case. |

AI-generated comments are review input, not an acceptance or refusal decision. Open Source Europe is a distinct host; this page describes coordination with Lucas, not a transfer of its decision authority.

The OCE intake route includes the [OCE form](https://www.oceurope.org/apply) and the relevant Open Collective host profile.

## Confirm the host

* OCEF EUR: [foundation EUR profile](https://opencollective.com/oce-foundation-eur).
* OCEF USD: [foundation USD profile](https://opencollective.com/oce-foundation-usd).
* OSE: [Open Source Europe application](https://opencollective.com/europe/apply), a distinct host.

Do not reject an OCEF application solely because it is outside Europe. Review purpose, structure and practical funding conditions.

## Review and follow up

1. Laura gathers the relevant information and reviews the application. For an open-source project that applied to the wrong host, coordinate referral to Lucas and Open Source Europe.
2. Check completeness and run initiative review. Decide whether the available information supports acceptance or refusal under the applicable host's process, or whether further information is needed.
3. If information is missing, send a focused request explaining what is needed.
4. Laura and Ivan review applications together during their Tuesday call. They allocate messages case by case: sometimes they split the replies; sometimes Laura handles all replies. Make the next action and its owner clear before sending, and check existing exchanges to avoid duplicate responses.
5. Communicate the decision or next step. Laura updates the shared application record with the outcome and the reasons for acceptance or refusal, or the information still needed. For Open Source Europe, Laura also informs Lucas when the collective is accepted or refused.
6. Following OCE acceptance, complete activation under the appropriate OCE host and retain the collective's platform link. Track practical onboarding and any grant-agreement work separately. OSE activation remains under its own host process.

Use the [contact routes in the onboarding guide](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/the-onboarding-call#choose-the-contact-route) for call ownership and Lucas's participation in open-source onboarding.

## When admission is complete

**Admission is complete when the collective has been accepted and activated under OCE’s hosting on Open Collective.** A public profile alone is not sufficient: check that it is active under the correct OCE host and currency.

A specific agreement is not systematically signed by every collective as part of admission. Collectives that will receive grants through OCE require a specific agreement; follow the [mandate-agreement procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/creation-and-sending-of-mandate-agreements) for its scope and preparation. General hosting terms remain applicable.

Keep these outcomes distinct in the case record:

* **Admission:** accepted and activated under OCE’s hosting.
* **Practical onboarding:** guidance provided, questions and next actions recorded.
* **Grant agreement, where applicable:** prepared and signed under its own procedure.

An active hosted profile does not by itself establish that a grant agreement is signed or that the requirements for a grant transaction have been met.

## Administrator minimum

Collectives are expected to have at least two genuinely active administrators, primarily to ensure continuity. Adding a second name solely to meet the requirement does not provide that assurance.

A project genuinely run by one person may be accepted with one administrator following a documented assessment of the risk, clear responsibility, a workable continuity arrangement and appropriate expense controls. Where the one-administrator exception has been accepted, the sole administrator may submit and approve their own expense. OCE then performs its usual checks before payment: supporting documents, connection to the project and compliance with the applicable funding conditions. No additional independent approval within the collective is required for that expense.

Record any exception in the existing J1-05 exceptions register, including the reason, the authorised decision-maker and the conditions for review. Two administrators do not by themselves establish independent financial control.

## Shared application record

Laura keeps the existing “Application Follow-Up” document in Superhuman Docs up to date. Continue using Gwen's document rather than creating a parallel tracker.

Keep each entry concise and useful for the next review:

* Identify the collective and the relevant host, with a link to its platform record where available.
* Record its current status and any outstanding information.
* Record acceptance or refusal and the reasons for the decision.
* Keep the next action and responsible person clear.
* Link to supporting exchanges or form responses where useful, rather than copying the full conversation.

The register summarises progress and decisions. Open Collective remains the reference for the collective's actual hosting and activation status; Freshdesk retains the correspondence, and forms and Slack provide review inputs. If the register and those sources disagree, Laura clarifies the position with the people handling the application and updates the record before it is relied on.

Application assessments and decision reasons belong in the team's restricted working record, not in this handbook.

## Planned centralisation for Open Source Europe

For Open Source Europe, the intended improvement is to centralise application responses in Slack so that the team no longer needs to consult Typeform separately, while retaining Freshdesk for supplementary exchanges. This is a target workflow, not a completed migration. Continue checking the applicable form until its responses are reliably available through the agreed route. This change to the information-gathering route does not replace Laura's updates to the shared application record.

## Application response and follow-up

Provide a first response from the team within seven business days of receiving the application. This is not a commitment to a final acceptance decision within that period. Subsequent discussion, requests for information, reminders and any closure are handled case by case. No fixed automatic closure deadline is adopted; the historical two-week template must not be treated as a general closure rule.

## References

Use the [operational RACI](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle), [onboarding conversation guide](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/the-onboarding-call) and [current-source question guide](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/question-chatgpt). Signing powers, access and specialist validations remain separate.


# Run an onboarding conversation

Help the collective understand its next steps and confirm the practical arrangement.

## Purpose

Help the collective understand how to operate with OCE and what to do next. This conversation supports practical onboarding; it is distinct from completion of admission.

**Admission is complete when the collective is accepted and activated under OCE’s hosting on Open Collective.** A specific signed agreement is not a universal admission requirement. It is required for collectives that will receive grants through OCE; follow the [mandate-agreement procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/creation-and-sending-of-mandate-agreements).

## Choose the contact route

**Laura assesses the project’s potential impact and funding prospects during application triage and decides whether to proactively offer a call.** Tailor the initial guidance to the project:

* **Ambitious projects, assessed in terms of potential impact and funding prospects:** Laura proactively offers and leads the call, explores the project’s needs and owns the follow-up.
* **Other projects:** Ivan provides guidance by email and offers an optional call. If the collective takes up the offer, Ivan leads the call. He owns the follow-up.

Once a collective is accepted, Laura handles onboarding calls for larger or ambitious projects and Ivan for smaller projects. For open-source projects, Lucas also participates in every onboarding call. Confirm his participation when arranging the call and use the correct host's guidance.

A proactive invitation is an offer, not a mandatory call. These routes describe how OCE provides guidance; they do not add an admission criterion. Assess admission under the [application procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review).

Use the conversation guidance below when a call takes place. For email guidance, cover the relevant practical points in writing and keep the next action clear.

## Prepare

Read the application and prior exchanges. Confirm the host, case owner, open questions and the guidance applicable to the group. Use [operational checks](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/operational-checklist-mandatory-before-action) for consequential instructions.

## Suggested conversation

1. Introduce yourself and explain the purpose of the conversation.
2. Invite the group to describe its work and what it needs.
3. Explain the distinction between OCE, the collective and the platform.
4. Walk through a collective page, contribution and expense request using a suitable public or demonstration example.
5. Explain documentation, approvals, privacy and any grant reporting obligations.
6. Confirm unanswered questions and who will act next.

Use plain language, pause for questions and check understanding. Do not require someone to turn on a camera simply to create rapport. Avoid examples that imply arrangements unavailable to this host.

## Before closing

Explain the adopted [administrator and application rules](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review), [mandate scope](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/creation-and-sending-of-mandate-agreements) and [payment procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/payment-processing-and-disbursements). The first application response is due within seven business days; it is not a final acceptance deadline. Payment execution is due within seven business days after collective-administrator approval, subject to a blocking issue and notification. Provider arrival time is additional. Do not promise fixed processing weekdays.

## Record the result

Keep a short note of the arrangement, outstanding documents, owner and next action in the existing case record. Send the relevant pages from the [public guide](https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/) when communicating with the collective.

## A practical walkthrough the group can repeat

Use the [public platform guide](https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/what-we-offer/online-platform) or the current public guide navigation. Explain each step in text as well as on screen.

| Step                | Check understanding without creating a real transaction                               |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Find the collective | Ask the person to identify its name and host.                                         |
| Review privacy      | Explain public titles and display names, and where payment information belongs.       |
| Read the budget     | Ask what is received, what is already committed and what remains uncertain.           |
| Prepare an expense  | Identify the document and approval needed; stop before submitting a practice request. |
| Get help            | Check that the person can find the expense link and OCE contact route.                |

Let the participant choose whether to follow along, read later or ask for another format. Record unanswered questions and the owner of each follow-up. The conversation is complete when the next real action is clear and unanswered questions have an owner; every screen need not be demonstrated. Record this separately from hosting activation and any grant-agreement status.

## References

Use the [administrator and application rules](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review), [payment procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/payment-processing-and-disbursements) and [mandate scope](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/creation-and-sending-of-mandate-agreements). Contract/template validation is tracked separately in [documentation decisions and remaining validations](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce/brand).


# Review freezing and closure

Separate a temporary protective action from final treatment of funds.

## Establish the reason

Record the issue, evidence, affected activity, urgency and decision needed. A documentation gap, inactivity, suspected misconduct and a contractual breach are different situations.

## Before changing access or activity

Check the agreement, authority and proportionate action. Escalate legal or material risk through [risk and escalation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/risk-and-compliance). Communicate the reason and next step through the appropriate channel where permitted.

## Temporary restriction

Record what is paused, why, who authorised it, what is needed for review and the next review date. Keep evidence and fund records intact.

## Inactive collectives

Decision confirmed by JF on 14 September 2026. Both conditions must be met:

* No incoming or outgoing transactions for 24 consecutive months.
* Repeated communications to the collective have received no response.

Document the transaction history and the communication attempts, then send a final request for a response. If the collective remains unresponsive, initiate termination with 30 days' written notice in accordance with the applicable hosting agreement and its notice provisions. Inactivity alone does not automatically freeze the collective or reallocate its funds.

Handle any remaining balance, outstanding expenses and other assets under the applicable termination provisions, subject to applicable law and any required third-party approvals. Retain the final contact attempt, termination notice, decision and resulting records.

This process concerns an identified collective. Unidentified incoming funds follow the separate procedure linked below. The [published hosting template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vS2jTb55T-kXHDPLNWVg4xUuMGmediT9VBqwsNpdQA8geRpcPsyYvfPggwJ6iZaPw/pub) reviewed on 24 September 2026 includes the matching inactivity provision. Before applying it to an existing initiative, check its applicable agreement, effective date and any required notification or approval.

## Closure and remaining funds

Do not treat retention, reallocation or closure without transfer as an ordinary automatic outcome. The consolidated audit requires a contractual or legal basis and formal decision for these actions. A platform control does not supply that authority.

Record outstanding agreements, expenses, reports and the authorised treatment of remaining funds before closing the case. For unidentified money, use [the separate holding process](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/unclaimed-or-unreconciliable-funds).

## Source and review

Operational update: 14 September 2026. JF confirmed the cumulative inactivity criteria and final-contact/30-day termination process above. This resolves that operational decision in audit V05; it does not establish specialist validation of every freezing or closure scenario.


# Review an initiative

Document mission, structure, people and funding before a decision.

## Trigger and inputs

Use this review for a new application or a material change to an existing initiative. Gather the application, public profile, legal status if any, team information, activities, geography, budget and expected funding sources.

## Standard review

1. Confirm the intended host and the public-benefit purpose.
2. Compare the application with its public presence and supporting material.
3. Understand who administers the group and how decisions are made.
4. Check the proposed funding and payment routes.
5. Record missing information and the next action.

There is no automatic Europe-only eligibility limit for OCE Foundation. A lack of incorporation does not itself make an initiative unsuitable; use [the informal-group review](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/due-diligence-for-unregistered-groups).

## Enhanced review

Additional checks may be needed where the activity, jurisdiction, funder, payment route or conflicting information creates a material concern. Identify the actual concern and proportionate evidence needed. Seek specialist advice when the issue is legal or financial.

Do not equate a sensitive context or a limited public presence with wrongdoing. Consider whether publicity itself creates a safety risk.

## Output and decision

Record the evidence checked, findings, unresolved questions, recommendation, decision-maker and decision date in the restricted case record. Keep personal documents in Drive or the appropriate restricted system, not in a general handbook page.

Use [risk and escalation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/risk-and-compliance) for unresolved concerns and [application review](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review) for the workflow.

## Source and review

Checked on 24 September 2026. First triage and operational responsibilities (A01) and the administrator rule (A02) were adopted on 14 September. Use the [RACI adopted on 14 September 2026](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle) and [application procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review); specialist review remains case-specific.


# Review an informal or unregistered group

Adapt the evidence to the group while keeping its people and funds accountable.

Informal groups are part of OCE’s mission. This is the reference page for their review; the former parallel handling page now points here.

## Understand the group

* Identify its purpose, activities and intended community benefit.
* Establish who is responsible for administration and decisions.
* Record its location and relevant funding and payout jurisdictions.
* Understand expected funding and whether an agreement or grant imposes specific conditions.

Verify identity through the appropriate private process. Do not require a legal name or identity document to be public merely because OCE needs to verify it.

## Where evidence is difficult to obtain

Ask for a short explanation, relevant links, a conversation or other appropriate corroboration. Record why a particular document cannot be provided and what remains uncertain. An alternative must be assessed rather than invented by the reviewer.

## Funding and payment route

Do not automatically route a group to OSE, require incorporation or reject it solely because it expects a substantial grant. Establish the actual legal and operational arrangement with the competent reviewers.

If the grantee and the proposed payee differ, pause the affected payment and obtain a documented decision on that route. See [grant lifecycle](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures).

## Administrator minimum

The [administrator rule](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review#administrator-minimum) sets two active administrators as the default and allows a documented exception for a genuinely individual project. Assess responsibility, continuity and OCE’s usual pre-payment checks of the administrator’s expenses; record the exception in J1-05 with its reason, decision-maker and review conditions.

The sole administrator may submit and approve their own expense. OCE checks the supporting documents, connection to the project and applicable funding conditions before payment.

## Open policy points

The organisation checklist and documented exceptional personal-account/intermediary routes were confirmed on 14 September 2026 in [the grant lifecycle](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures). Apply that evidence checklist and retain the case decision. This is not a blanket authorisation for personal-account payments. Specialist validation and the Organisation/Vendor profile question remain separate in [documentation decisions and remaining validations](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce/brand).

## Source and review

Checked on 24 September 2026 against the decisions of 14 September: administrator exception A02 and the operational onward-grant checklist. The administrator exception does not itself authorise a personal-account payment. Remaining specialist validations are listed in [documentation decisions and remaining validations](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce/brand).


# Manage the grant lifecycle

Take a grant from announcement to evidenced receipt, delivery and closure.

#### Purpose and responsibilities

Use this procedure when a collective announces funding it expects to receive through OCE, usually by email. The collective introduces OCE to the donor foundation; Laura coordinates the contract and transfer arrangements with the foundation.

**Laura owns the grant file and this procedure.** She reviews funding conditions before OCE commits, coordinates the agreements, tracks obligations and follows the dossier through to closure.

**Ivan prepares the operational receipt and allocation, maintains transaction evidence and executes authorised operations. CFO retains financial review and conclusions.** The collective supplies project information and delivers its agreed activities and reporting contributions.

Use the [operational RACI](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle) for decision routes. File ownership does not confer signing authority. JF handles material commitments and genuine exceptions; reserved matters follow the applicable governance route.

#### At a glance

| Stage                  | Lead                                                | Result needed                                                                                        |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Announcement           | Laura                                               | Identified grant, collective, donor, amount, currency, purpose and timetable                         |
| Conditions review      | Laura, with financial or specialist input as needed | Obligations understood; open questions and required decisions visible                                |
| Agreements             | Laura coordinates                                   | Coherent donor and collective agreements; required approvals and signatures identified and completed |
| Transfer preparation   | Laura hands over to Ivan                            | Expected receipt can be recognised and allocated under the agreed conditions                         |
| Receipt and allocation | Ivan; CFO for financial review                      | Actual funds matched to the file, discrepancies addressed and collective informed                    |
| Reporting and closure  | Laura; CFO for financial information                | Obligations evidenced, outstanding matters resolved and closure recorded                             |

#### 1. Qualify the arrangement

Create or update the grant’s record in OCE Grants as soon as the collective announces the funding. Laura ensures that the record exists and has a named owner. Capture the collective and platform link, donor foundation and contact, expected amount and currency, purpose, timetable and next action. Obtain the introduction to the foundation and link the relevant correspondence.

Identify the legal recipient, beneficiary and intended activities. Confirm whether OCE is receiving a grant, administering a fund or processing an onward grant. Do not infer the legal model from a platform profile.

Use [Forms of support and administrative contributions](/oc-europe-internal-doc/the-foundation/forms-of-support-and-administrative-contributions) to identify the support arrangement, scope and contribution calculation. Funding routes can cross the support models; the applicable agreement determines the obligations.

**Ready for review:** the parties and intended funding route are identified, with missing information assigned to an owner.

For public funding or a nonstandard structure, obtain the appropriate case decision. For Ma Earth, use the actual upstream agreement and legal review; definitive legal characterisation remains unresolved.

#### 2. Review documents and authority

**Review the funder’s conditions**

Laura gathers the proposal, budget, funding conditions, due-diligence material and draft agreement. Identify:

* What the grant may fund, the project period and any restrictions.
* What OCE is committing to and what the collective must deliver.
* Payment amounts, currencies, tranches and conditions for release.
* Reports and other deliverables, their recipients and deadlines.
* Amendment, unused-fund and repayment provisions, where applicable.
* Questions requiring financial treatment, specialist advice or an exception decision.

The CFO reviews financial questions within his role. Laura obtains the appropriate decision on unresolved commitments or specialist issues. Record the answer, decision-maker and supporting reference; a conversation alone does not establish that a condition is resolved.

**Prepare coherent agreements**

Check that the agreement with the foundation and the mandate with the collective describe compatible purposes, obligations, timelines and financial terms. A mandate is required for collectives receiving grants through OCE. Follow [agreement preparation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/creation-and-sending-of-mandate-agreements) for templates, checks, signature and storage.

Identify the authorised signatories and obtain the applicable approvals. Link the signed versions in the restricted grant record.

**Ready for commitment:** relevant conditions have been reviewed and required decisions are recorded. A draft or a sent signature request is not a signed agreement. Keep unresolved items visible and pause the affected commitment or action; continue unaffected preparation.

#### 3. Track the grant

**Every grant must be registered in OCE Grants.** It is the operational reference for the grant’s follow-up, deadlines and next actions. Laura ensures registration and keeps the record current throughout the grant lifecycle.

Record each reporting deadline, project end date and other contractual deadline, with the person responsible for the action. Add expected payment dates and the next action where known. If a date is not yet known, record the missing information and who will obtain it; do not invent a deadline.

Update the record when an agreement is signed or amended, a payment is received, a report is submitted or an obligation is completed. Keep submission evidence linked, and track remaining obligations until closure. For Myriad requests, also follow [Coordinate Myriad USA](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/myriad-usa).

Use Open Collective for collective, fund and transaction records, and restricted Drive folders for signed agreements and supporting evidence. Link these records from OCE Grants rather than creating a competing grant register. See [Tools and records — grant tracking](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce#grant-tracking-next-cycle-delivery).

Use the control sheet below within the OCE Grants dossier. If a dedicated field is unavailable, link a restricted note from that dossier. This procedure does not presume that every checklist item has a dedicated application field or that automatic reminders are configured.

**Prepare the transfer and hand over to Ivan**

Laura coordinates the transfer arrangements with the foundation. Before the expected transfer, give Ivan:

* The collective, correct OCE entity, currency and destination account or validated route.
* Donor identity, expected amount, tranche and expected receipt date.
* The payment reference or other information needed to match the receipt.
* Links to signed agreements, contribution terms and relevant restrictions.
* Any outstanding condition, uncertainty or decision affecting receipt or allocation.

Ivan checks that the information is sufficient to recognise and allocate the receipt and flags missing operational details to Laura. Laura keeps ownership of funder questions. CFO reviews financial uncertainty where needed.

**Ready for transfer:** the required agreement and conditions are in place, the destination and matching information are clear, and the operational handover is recorded. If funds arrive unexpectedly, record the receipt and resolve missing information before treating the grant as ready for allocation or use.

**Grant control sheet**

For each line, record **complete, pending or not applicable**, with the evidence link, owner and next action/date where needed. Explain why a line is not applicable. These are checklist values, not presumed software statuses.

| Check                        | Evidence or result to retain                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Grant identified             | Collective, donor/contact, legal recipient, amount, currency, purpose and timetable       |
| Conditions reviewed          | Restrictions, obligations, reporting dates and resolved or open questions                 |
| Agreements ready             | Required approvals, authorised signatures and links to signed donor/collective agreements |
| Receipt prepared             | Expected transfer details, contribution terms and handover to Ivan                        |
| Funds received and allocated | Actual receipt, platform references, allocation and any discrepancy resolution            |
| Collective informed          | Confirmation of actual receipt/allocation and relevant remaining restrictions             |
| Obligations tracked          | Owner and deadline for each report, deliverable or amendment                              |
| Closure evidenced            | Reporting evidence, financial position and treatment of remaining obligations or funds    |

The checklist records the evidence; it does not replace the agreements or confer approval.

#### 4. Receive and allocate

Ivan matches the actual bank receipt to the agreement, expected transfer and platform record. Check the payer/reference, amount, currency and tranche. Record discrepancies such as a partial receipt, unexpected charges or an unidentified transfer, and route them to Laura or CFO as appropriate. Do not mark an expected receipt as received solely because the donor says it has been sent.

Follow [Incoming transfers](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives) and its [grant receipt checklist](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives#grant-receipt-checklist-net-allocation-and-administrative-contribution): verify the signed mandate’s contribution terms, credit the collective net, manually record the administrative contribution on the correct operating budget, and link and reconcile both entries without an additional automatic platform fee.

Ivan retains the transaction references and evidence. Laura ensures the collective is informed of the actual receipt and allocation, including any unresolved issue or restriction. CFO retains financial review; operational entry alone is not an independent financial conclusion.

**Receipt complete:** the actual funds are matched, allocation is evidenced, discrepancies are resolved or explicitly tracked, and the collective has been informed. Receipt does not remove restrictions on use.

#### 5. Review onward payments

For an onward grant to an organisation, retain:

1. Organisation registration documents or bylaws.
2. A signed request identifying the purpose and intended use of the grant.
3. Bank account holder evidence.
4. Evidence of the representative's identity and authority to act.
5. The grant agreement.

**Exceptional situations — internal handling**

Where there is no legal organisation, payment may exceptionally be made directly to an individual's account. Document the absence of a legal structure, the beneficiary and project, the individual's identity and role, account ownership, purpose, applicable agreement and the case decision. Record why standard organisation documents cannot be provided and the evidence supporting the arrangement.

Payment may also be made through an intermediary. In addition to the beneficiary/project documentation, collect the intermediary's bank account evidence and all applicable supporting documents for the intermediary, including its identity or registration, representative authority and agreement establishing its role. Document the relationship between beneficiary and intermediary and the intended transfer and use of funds.

Keep personal and banking evidence in restricted records and retain the payment trail. These exceptional routes require a documented case; they do not determine the separate Organisation/Vendor platform-profile question, which remains deferred.

#### 6. Report and close

Laura records each obligation in OCE Grants with its owner and deadline. Coordinate narrative reporting with the collective/project owner and financial information with CFO; Ivan supplies transaction evidence. Link submitted reports and submission confirmations. Retain acceptance evidence where the agreement requires it.

Record amendments and changes to dates, budget or conditions in the same dossier. Update the relevant obligations and inform those implementing the change.

Before closing, Laura checks that:

* Required reports and deliverables have supporting evidence.
* CFO has reviewed the financial position, with unresolved differences made explicit.
* Remaining funds, repayment requirements and other obligations have been addressed under the agreement.
* The closure outcome and evidence are recorded and accessible to the relevant team.

**A transfer or a submitted report alone does not close the grant.** Keep the dossier open where a required action remains.

#### Maintain this procedure

Laura keeps this procedure aligned with the operating process, with Ivan for operational steps and CFO for financial controls. Review the affected guidance when a funding route, contractual requirement, tool or responsibility changes, or when a recurring error exposes a gap. Use [Review operational records](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce/oce-periodic-cleanup) to identify outstanding work and outdated guidance.

Keep this public page focused on the process. Store agreements, personal or banking information and case evidence in restricted records.

Specialist legal/tax validation, contract-specific characterisation and the Organisation/Vendor question remain separate matters tracked in [documentation decisions and remaining validations](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce/brand).

See [U.S. funding](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/receiving-funds-from-the-u.s.), [Myriad USA](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/myriad-usa) and [GSF](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/gsf) for route-specific workflows.


# Choose a U.S. funding route

Distinguish direct foundation grants from the Myriad donation route.

## Confirm the entity first

OCEF and OSE are separate legal entities. Do not use one entity’s agreement, account or eligibility documentation for the other.

## U.S. private foundation

Check whether the funder can use OCE’s current Equivalency Determination documentation. Obtain the current evidence and confirm that it applies to the intended grant. The existence of an ED is not an automatic approval for every foundation or grant.

## Myriad USA

For an eligible arrangement using Myriad, Laura coordinates the operational relationship, grant request and reporting. Follow [the Myriad procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/myriad-usa). Do not ask collectives to manage the Myriad relationship directly.

## Direct contribution

A direct contribution to the platform or OCE account does not, by itself, establish U.S. tax deductibility. Confirm the intended route before instructions are sent.

## OSE status to check

The reviewed email thread confirms that OSE needs its own application and agreement with Myriad. Laura’s 7 September message asks whether setup should remain on hold. No later approval is established by that thread. Do not document the OSE route as active or automatically move a collective to OCEF to obtain it.

For every route, retain the agreement, entity, receipt, allocation and reporting evidence.

# Receive European funding

Check the funder’s conditions and the applicable legal arrangement.

## Qualify the opportunity

Identify the funder, intended activity, legal recipient, amount, currency and deadline. Check whether the funder accepts the proposed hosted arrangement. For public funding, apply the case-by-case decision route below.

## Public funding

OCE has not yet accepted public funding. Public funding remains an exploratory opportunity for hosted collectives and for OCE itself, with previous exploration involving Open Source Europe. Assess each opportunity individually; this is not an established service or a blanket eligibility commitment. JF gives the go-ahead before OCE commits to a case. Review the funder’s conditions and the applicable legal arrangement for that opportunity.

## Agreement and receipt

Review the agreement before commitment. Verify the signatory’s authority and any required mandate. Provide the correct receiving instructions, retain the signed documents and follow [receipt and allocation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives).

## Tax statements

JF confirmed on 14 September 2026 that European tax-deductible donation arrangements are exceptional, assessed on request for substantial amounts. No numeric threshold has been established in this decision. Assess the country and available route before providing donation instructions or tax assurances. The U.S. donation route is Myriad USA, subject to that route's conditions and the donor's tax circumstances; citizenship or payment origin alone does not establish deductibility.

Do not infer country-specific deductibility from OCE’s public utility status or an ecosystem partnership. The audit explicitly suspends the old blanket KBF recognition claim. Obtain the competent tax or legal confirmation before making such a statement.

## Follow-up

Track purpose restrictions, reporting dates and changes in the project record. Coordinate financial information through the agreed financial-control route.

Return to **Manage the grant lifecycle** in the navigation for the common checklist.

## Source and review

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identified A04, A09 and V07. The mandate scope A04 and the public-funding decision route A09 were confirmed on 14 September 2026. V07 tax validation remains separate. Record the approved text and effective date before changing the corresponding operating rule.


# Prepare a mandate agreement

Use the correct approved template, verify authority and retain the signed record.

## Before drafting

Confirm why a mandate is needed for this arrangement, the legal entity, the activity and the approved template. Apply the funding-based scope confirmed below.

## When a mandate is required

A mandate agreement is mandatory for collectives receiving grants through OCE. It is optional for collectives receiving only crowdfunding donations without particular conditions. Review other funding arrangements, including contributions with particular conditions, case by case to determine the appropriate agreement. The general hosting terms remain applicable when a mandate is optional.

## Workflow

1. Obtain the instruction and identify the case owner.
2. Select the approved template for the correct entity: [OCEF templates](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Zs26YrAQ5vav4btWBCuLLb2RMcK3orAE) or the separately authorised OSE route.
3. Complete only the required project and signatory details. Verify names and authority privately.
4. Review the scope, purpose, parties and required checks. Escalate deviations from the approved template.
5. Obtain the required approval and send for signature through the authorised signature system.
6. Save the signed document in the collective’s restricted Drive folder and link it to the platform agreement record.
7. Record the effective dates, expiry if any, and remaining obligations from the signed document.
8. Make the signed administrative-contribution clause available to the person processing receipts: percentage and calculation base or fixed amount, currency, tranche/timing rules, and any valid documented amendment or exemption. Do not assume the template's default rate applies. At receipt, use the [grant allocation checklist](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives#grant-receipt-checklist-net-allocation-and-administrative-contribution).

## Controls

Do not rewrite legal clauses from memory. Do not assume that two names, a particular end-date setting or a historical Board list is correct for every agreement. Check the actual mandate and delegation.

Screen relevant parties through the established review process and resolve material questions before signature. Keep identity evidence and signatures out of public pages.

## Completion

The record should contain the approved version, signatures, date, applicable entity and link to the platform record. A sent signature request is not a completed agreement.

## Source and review

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identified A04, A02 and V10 for decision or specialist validation. The funding-based scope of A04 was confirmed on 14 September 2026 above; A02 is recorded in the administrator rule. Specialist validation of the mandate template and signing authority remains separate.


# Coordinate Myriad USA

Track the grant request, allocation and reporting as one cycle.

**Operational coordination: Laura.** OCE manages the relationship with Myriad; collectives and beneficiaries do not contact Myriad directly under the documented workflow.

## Before a request

Confirm the OCE legal entity, eligible project, intended route and applicable agreement. Verify the current contact and individual portal access. Do not store access codes or authentication links in this handbook.

JF confirmed on 7 October 2026 that the initial agreement signed with Myriad covers subsequent requests. The agreement is retained in the Myriad USA folder in Drive. Refer to that existing agreement when preparing a request, alongside the request-specific purpose, conditions and reporting requirements. This confirmation concerns the agreement with Myriad; it does not settle the documentation or approval of an onward transfer to another legal entity.

Use the **Grants Portal** to submit regranting requests from Myriad USA to OCE, and the **Fund Portal** to manage and monitor the Myriad fund. Their links and uses are set out below. The **Donor Portal** serves donor activity; it is a separate route.

## Grant request

To submit a regranting request from Myriad USA to OCE, use the [Myriad USA Grants Portal](https://www.grantinterface.com/Home/Logon?urlkey=myriadusa). Sign in with your authorised individual account. This is the request portal for this transfer route, rather than the Fund Portal or Donor Portal.

To start a new request:

1. Sign in and open the portal dashboard.
2. Click **Apply**.
3. Enter **`friends`** to access the application process for a new regranting request.

Laura prepares the request before transfer, including the project narrative and end date. Save the submitted version and its confirmation with the project evidence. Check that the purpose matches the intended allocation.

**After submitting the request to Myriad, record it in OCE’s internal grant-tracking application.** Laura ensures that the submitted request is entered there, with its submission date and a reference to the submitted version and confirmation, so it can be followed through receipt, allocation and reporting.

## Fund management and monitoring

Use the [Myriad Fund Portal — Fund Advisor](https://kbfus.fcsuite.com/erp/portal/fundadvisor?profile_id=68717) to manage and monitor the grants and funds held in the Myriad fund. Sign in with your authorised account to:

* Check how much is held in the fund.
* Follow incoming funds and grant activity.
* Export CSV files for tracking and financial review.

Use the Grants Portal above when starting a new regranting request from Myriad USA to OCE. A fund balance or expected incoming amount does not establish that OCE has received the money; confirm the actual receipt through the workflow below.

## Receipt and allocation

Laura identifies the grant and supplies allocation context. Ivan records the actual receipt against the correct collective and currency. Financial review checks the bank, platform and grant evidence through the agreed control route.

## Reporting

Treat the project end date as a tracked obligation. Record the reporting deadline, owner, status and submission evidence. Obtain the collective’s update, explain activities and changes, prepare the report and retain confirmation of submission.

If the project will not finish as expected, raise the change before the deadline and record any agreed amendment.

## Working record

Keep project, route, expected funds, request date, narrative, end date, receipt, allocation, reporting status, next action and evidence links together. Use OCE’s internal grant-tracking application for this operational follow-up and link the supporting evidence.

## Keep instructions current

Use current payment instructions confirmed for the intended fund. Avoid stale contacts, copied bank details and historic transfer-frequency promises.

## Source and review

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. Consolidated audit D09 and V13; [agreement thread](https://mail.google.com/mail/#all/1a0490ca968e5597). The overarching route priority remains a validation item; this page preserves the documented OCEF operational cycle.

Portal references and uses confirmed by JF on 1 October 2026: Grants Portal for regranting requests from Myriad USA to OCE; Fund Portal for fund management, balances, incoming funds and CSV exports.

Internal grant-tracking step confirmed by JF on 1 October 2026: enter the request in OCE’s internal grant application after submission to Myriad.

Laura’s documented role covers complex-project delivery. Ivan supplies routine execution and operational evidence. Financial treatment and controlled reporting require the competent financial review. JF decides material executive matters within authority.

Record completed outputs, reports, amendments and remaining obligations. Capture a reusable lesson in GitBook only after its scope and validity are established.

# Route projects by complexity

Separate routine execution, complex coordination and material decisions.

## Working categories

| Category       | Practical characteristics                                                                   |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Standard       | Established workflow, ordinary documentation and clear funding/payout route.                |
| Complex        | Specific funder obligations, several parties, tailored reporting or a nonstandard workflow. |
| Strategic fund | Programme-wide coordination, significant governance implications or complex regranting.     |

The earlier matrix used monetary bands. Do not use those bands alone to approve a project or establish signing authority. A project can be strategically or legally complex at any amount.

## Routing record

Record the category, reason, case owner, execution responsibilities and next action. Laura reviews every incoming application first, then assigns it to herself or Ivan, or refers the appropriate misdirected open-source application to Lucas for OSE.

## A genuine exception

Identify the actual departure from the applicable arrangement. A host redirection, incomplete file or high amount alone is not enough. Define the affected commitment and obtain the required decision before relying on an exception.

Use the [lightweight exception register](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/10XFG2WgtWxz-c9X0kbn-sA2OPhSWVOrEGbI_m1x5z9M/edit) as the workstream reference. The [plan reviewed on 22 September 2026](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ghToLzMnkuzCyowZi0sh6aBz3jMc5RPU1uU-AOBT3Qs/edit) marks J1-05 complete and records documented use. Continue to track conditions and review dates in that register; completion of the tool does not close individual cases or authorise a new deviation. The archived broad checklist is historical.

## Reassess when facts change

If the beneficiary, legal arrangement, funding or payment route changes, review the classification and authority again. A previous classification is not permanent approval for expanded activity.

## Source and review

Operational responsibilities adopted by JF on 14 September 2026: [operational RACI adopted on 14 September 2026](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle).
